analysis:
This PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and the GLM-5 reasoning-controls table row around line 1147 (head). The visible head text (units :6 and :7) is truncated before the changed lines, so the reasoning-controls row was assessed from the patch excerpt, which is itself truncated. The patch says reasoning:null and null reasoning members are unset, reasoning.summary and reasoning.generate_summary accept auto/concise/detailed as no-ops, and other reasoning members are refused. The surrounding visible content is unchanged: App Attest endpoint-resumption candidate (TB-011, T-053), the drain barrier, the register fields and the model_autopilot state.

No security controls, wire fields, authorization gates or trust assumptions in those visible sections are altered, and the doc does not weaken any TB-002 or TB-011 claim. The resumption text still says the provider does not grant local trust, that backend policy is platform-owned and that the exchange is not a bearer grant. It stays consistent with the threat model's T-053 boundary and with the TB-011 statement that the platform rechecks retained evidence.

The reasoning-control change documents provider-side prompt-policy parsing in GLM5NextPromptPolicy.swift. That source is not in the supplied units, so I cannot confirm the doc matches the implementation. A mismatch would at worst be doc drift, not a demonstrated vulnerability. One residual question for later passes is whether the accepted no-op summary values are handled by the Swift parser with bounded input, so that malformed reasoning members are refused as stated. No finding is supported by the supplied evidence.
